newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Vulkan chief blames state for collapse.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Vulkan chief blames state for collapse.

text.p: The former head of collapsed German shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan AG, Friedrich Hennemann, said on Tuesday that the ruling coalition of the city state of Bremen was to blame for the shipyards collapse.

Hennemann also denied allegations by former fellow board members that he had blocked attempts to improve productivity at the shipyards, saying that productivity in the Vulkan shipyards was no worse than in any other shipyards in Germany.
Hennemann also said it was incorrect that he had gone against expert advice regarding the construction of container ships.

His remarks coincided with word from European Union sources that the European Commission was expected to extend the probe into alleged misuse by Bremer Vulkan of 200 million marks ($132.5 million) in German subsidies.
Hennemann was speaking before a committee set up by the Bremen government to examine the reasons for the downfall of the shipyard, which declared bankruptcy in May.

He said the collapse of the yards could have been avoided if the politicians had wanted it, Hennemann said, and the shipyards could keep building if the situation was dealt with quickly and decisively.
Hennemann stepped down as chief executive of Bremer Vulkan in November 1995, and spent seven weeks in investigative custody during the summer.
Politicians attending the committee said that Hennemann's comments "passed reality by."

"As far as I'm concerned, that was Hennemann's hour for telling fairy stories," said the Christian Democrat Brigitte Dreyer, while the Green Party's Helga Truepel said that Hennemann's comments were about "building his own legend."
